name: Hud_ApplyWidgetRectangle
summary: Reads two position/size tuples from a widget's inner object, fills a rectangle, then writes a2/a3 into the tuples and a4/a5 into the rectangle, applying each via vtable calls and returning the last call's result.
notes: Vtable slot semantics (getters at 15 and 11, setters at 10, 14, 21, 22) are inferred from call pattern only; slot 21 is treated as an apply/set-rect call whose result is returned. The owning class is unknown, so self is void*. Local array v16 overlaps nothing; rect[1] and rect[3] stay uninitialized as in the original.

name: HudPanel_ReleaseReferences
summary: Releases two referenced HUD sub-objects (at +4 and +8 via ReleaseObjectReference on obj+4) and destroys the owned object at +0 through vtable slot 1, zeroing each field; returns the last step's result.
notes: Parameter type unknown, so modeled as int*. The return value follows the original: if the +8 branch is taken, eax is overwritten by ReleaseObjectReference, and if +0 is set, by the virtual call. Hex-Rays wrote the field-2 read into result before the null test, which is preserved.

name: Hud_ReadRectFromProperties
summary: Reads TOP/LEFT/WIDTH/HEIGHT integer properties from a HUD object and writes an int[4] rect {left, top, right, bottom} (right = left+width, bottom = top+height).
notes: a2 is a plain int array, not a declared class, so no field_names entries. Output order: a2[0]=left, a2[1]=top, a2[2]=right, a2[3]=bottom, inferred from the arithmetic. S_00692b80 is assumed to be declared in types/auto_classes.h. Callee ReadIntegerProperty is bound per the packet's bind line.

name: C_0082d410_InitFromEntry
summary: Resets this widget entry (font/size fields to defaults, clears flag byte), copies the source string substring via AssignStringSubstring, copies five trailing dword fields from the source, and returns this.
notes: Offsets 0x14/0x18 and 0x1C-0x2C are not declared fields, so accessed via CSF_AT. Hex-Rays 'a2[2]'/'a2[3]' indexing was resolved to the byte offsets in the disassembly (0x1C..0x2C). Field meanings are guesses. Return type int per Hex-Rays prototype. Stack arg a2 with ret 4 is modeled as __fastcall with unused edx.

name: Hud_CopyWidgetRange
summary: Iterates records of stride 0x30 from first up to last, resets each record's string from source (AssignStringSubstring full range) and copies five dwords from source+0x1C..+0x2C into the record at +0x1C..+0x2C; returns last.
notes: Record element is 0x30 bytes; C_0082d410 field layout unknown, so record fields are accessed via CSF_AT offsets. Source treated as uint32_t array (a3 is _DWORD*). Return value is always a2 (last). Pseudocode's a1[2].field_0008 indexing doesn't match the 0x30 stride in disassembly; the disassembly was followed.

name: Hud_CreateCenteredBorder

notes: Widget position and size slot names are inferred. Preserves pointer-valued return when content is absent and reloads widget pointers after calls.

name: CHud_InitializeConfiguredWidgets
summary: Resolves HUD widgets, applies configured geometry, color and texture scaling, and expands entry storage to 30 entries.
notes: Widget identities and the precise storage-growth operation are inferred; virtual calls preserve the supplied slots and argument counts.

name: Hud_UpdateAnimatedCounter
summary: Updates a HUD counter's text and animates its color between red and white when the scene flag is active.
notes: Owner class and widget virtual method names are unknown; raw offsets and virtual slots are used. Returns only the low byte of the scene state or final virtual call.

name: CHud_CopyBoundsFromSource
summary: Prepares the source object via sub_42E020, then copies two 2-dword pairs returned by its vtable slots 11 and 15 into CHud at +0x314..+0x320; returns the second pair pointer.
notes: Fixed the unknown type: the signature now uses CHud, the class name declared in auto_classes.h, instead of the Hex-Rays name C_00830a04. Fields at 0x314..0x320 are accessed via CSF_AT since they are not declared. Callee sub_42E020 is bound as CHud_PrepareSource but its real role is unknown. Pair semantics (min/max) are guessed from the layout. The vtable call results are unknown in meaning. Assumes the header declares CHud; if the gate still fails, the header uses a different name.

name: Hud_ScaleRectPositionAndSize
summary: Scales a rectangle (left, top, right, bottom) in place: position is scaled by one factor pair from 0x42DE60, size by a second pair, and the scaled height is returned.
notes: Semantics of 0x42DE60 are unknown; it fills two floats and its return is ignored, so the factor meaning is inferred from use. The callee was renamed to FillScaleFactorPair (packet allowed any name). __ftol2 is replaced by int64 casts; static_cast<int> from int64 is modular in C++20, matching the low-dword truncation. Original reads of a1[0]/a1[1] after the second callee call are preserved. The return value is the low dword of the scaled height, matching eax.

name: Hud_CopySourceLayoutState
summary: Pulls layout, state and a 64-byte block from a source accessor (a2) via vtable getters into the HUD object's fields at +0x2D4..+0x30C and returns the final query result (also stored at +0x308).
notes: The owning class id is unknown, so self is typed void* and all field accesses use CSF_AT with raw offsets. Slot numbers are byte offset / 4 (0x48->18, 0x50->20, 0x58->22, 0x64->25, 0x6C->27, 0x74->29). The 0x64 getter returns a pointer to a pointer: the 64-byte source block is read through it, and the destination pointer at +0x30C is read after that call, as in the disassembly. The 16-byte scratch buffer passed to slot 0x58 is uninitialized, as in the original. Meanings of the 4-dword groups (rects/colors) and the 64-byte block (possibly a 4x4 matrix) are guesses from the HUD module context. Stack layout and the single stack argument match ret 4 under __fastcall.

name: Hud_RefreshSceneOverlay
summary: If the overlay widget at +0x240 exists and the current scene menu context has state 2, sets the "I" tag, computes a 250x530 rect via sub_42F3B0, applies it to the widget, and returns the widget's slot-2 result; otherwise returns the scene context (or 0).
notes: Return value when the scene context exists but state != 2 is the context pointer itself (eax left over from GetSceneMenuContext), which is reproduced. Widget vtable slot typing is unknown (void* self); slot 0x3C and 0x50 return types assumed void since eax is ignored. Callee sub_42F3B0 named Hud_ComputeOverlayRect (signature kept). Scene context type unknown; accessed via CSF_AT at +0x78.

name: HudUpdateSceneMenuVisibility
summary: If the HUD's scene-menu context pointer (+0x24C) is set, flags it (byte +0x4C = 1) and, when the current scene reports a menu context, forwards the context to HudApplySceneMenuContext (tail call).
notes: Return value is 0 on the no-call paths (eax is zero there); on the tail-call path it returns sub_43A3E0's char result, which is kept as int. Self type is not declared, so offsets use CSF_AT. Callee 0x43A3E0 name is a guess.

name: HudCheckSceneMenuChanged
summary: Caches the current scene menu id/secondary value in the hud object; on first run also seeds extra cached fields, and returns 1 when the menu id changed since the last call, else 0.
notes: Hud object class unknown, so fields are accessed via CSF_AT with offsets 0x210-0x224. The vtable slot at +0xA0 (slot 40) on the object at menu context +0x38 is called with no arguments; its return type is assumed to be a 32-bit value. Return is a char holding 0/1, and the second GetSceneMenuContext call in the else-if branch is kept as in the original. The 0x218-0x210 cached zero fields are assumed to be plain uint32 stores. Semantics of the menu context fields (+0x20 id, +0x24 secondary, +0x38 subobject) are inferred from the disassembly, not from a named struct.

name: Hud_GetSignedVectorAngle
summary: Computes a signed angle for the 2D vector (a1[0], a1[2]) via sub_6AEE40; returns 0 when the length is <= epsilon.
notes: The packet bind for 0x6AEE40 is void, but the pseudocode and disassembly use its result in st0 as the function's double return. I deviated to a double-returning signature for that address so the value is preserved; reconcile with the codebase bind. Epsilon constant at 0x830674 is bound as float g_fEpsilon. Hook is a plain __stdcall (ret 4) with no this, as the packet requires.

name: Hud_RefreshDebugOverlay
summary: If the HUD object's overlay member exists and the global debug flag (byte +0x90C) is set, sets the 'G' overlay text, computes coordinates (230,530), repositions the overlay and returns the result of its virtual slot 2 call; otherwise returns the global pointer or 0.
notes: Overlay object type unknown, so virtual calls use CSF_AT(void**) slot dispatch (slots 15, 20, 2). The string at 0x830914 is bound as CSF_STR and assumed to be "G" per the pseudocode. Overlay object is re-read from this+0x240 before each call, matching the original. Return value on the flag-clear path is the global pointer from GetGlobalValue_8BC1E0, not 0. Hud_ComputeOverlayCoords is named by me; its bind signature is copied from the packet.

name: ReleaseHudInstance
summary: If the global HUD instance pointer is set, runs its teardown (sub_434800), frees it via Mem_Free, and nulls the global.
notes: C_00830a04 is not declared in types/auto_classes.h, so the instance is handled as void* and passed to sub_434800 directly. Null path in the original returns whatever eax held on entry; this returns 0, the only inexact part. Calling convention assumed __cdecl (no args, plain ret). The global is int32_t in data but holds a pointer, so it is converted through uintptr_t.

name: CHud_DispatchToResolvedControl
summary: Resolves a HUD sub-object for a request id via 0x42EBA0 and, if non-null, forwards it to 0x42F4F0 with flag 0.
notes: The C_00830a04 type name is not declared in types/auto_classes.h, so self is taken as void* to avoid redefining or inventing the struct. Callee 0x42F4F0 is __usercall taking a1 in edi; C++ cannot set edi, so the first argument is passed as 0 and the binding uses __cdecl. This behavioral gap may be flagged by the in-game diff. The hook is __fastcall with one stack arg (ret 4), matching the original.

name: Hud_GetSingleton
summary: Lazily allocates an 820-byte CHud object via Mem_Alloc, constructs it with the in-place initializer at 0x4355D0, caches it in g_Value_8afc78, and returns it (null if allocation fails).
notes: Assumes CHud is declared in types/auto_classes.h and CSF_FUNC/CSF_GLOBAL macros are provided by hook.h/globals.h. The callee 0x4355D0 is named Hud_ConstructInstance by me; its real role is unverified beyond it being called with the new object as ecx and returning a pointer-sized value. Calling convention of the hook assumed __cdecl with no stack args (ret 0).

name: Hud_FormatAndPlaceOverlayText
summary: printf-formats text into the HUD overlay widget at hud+0x240, scales a 2-int anchor point by two floats from Hud_ComputeScaleFactors, moves the widget there, and returns the widget's slot-2 result.
notes: Widget class at hud+0x240 is unknown, so vtable access uses CSF_AT(void**, ...). Slots used: 2 (+0x08), 15 (+0x3C, takes char*), 20 (+0x50, takes int32_t*); their meanings are guessed from the call patterns. The scaling now converts each int32 to double and multiplies by the float scale in double precision (fild of a dword followed by fmul of a float32 operand), so no precision is lost before truncation; the product is then truncated through int64 and stored as its low dword, matching the original's __ftol2 plus dword store. The original has no va_end call; __builtin_va_end is emitted as a no-op on x86 and is included only for correctness. Sub_42DE60 is unnamed in the packet; it is bound as Hud_ComputeScaleFactors (name chosen here, signature unchanged). The return type is int. Its name, behavior, and the widget's class are inferred.

name: Hud_TryReadIconProperty
summary: If the HUD object has the ICON property, stores its integer value into *a2, calls sub_42DF00(obj, a3) and returns 1; otherwise returns 0.
notes: Parameter a1 type S_00692b80 is not confirmed in auto_classes.h, so it is written as std::uint8_t*. Return is a char set via `xor al, al` / `mov al, 1`, so it is declared char. sub_42DF00 is bound with the packet signature (void*, int*) and receives a3 as its second argument. The `g_pszKey_ICON` global is read as a char* value on each use, as the original does.

name: C_008305f8_Destroy
summary: Destructor for C_008305f8: resets vtable to base C_00830630, destroys the embedded member at +8, sets vtable to C_008305f8, runs C_00860170_Construct on the base, and frees the object via Mem_Free when bit 0 of the argument is set; returns this.
notes: Callee sub_6C4A50 is named DestroyEmbeddedMember8 here (inferred from it being called on this+8 in a teardown sequence). The C_00860170_Construct call is bound by the packet's name even though it appears to act as a base teardown. Return value is this (eax = esi). Stack arg a2 is a char tested via bit 0; ret 4 matches the __fastcall signature with one stack argument.

name: S_0042ee00_AlignWidgetToScreenEdge
summary: Snaps an angle to a screen-edge orientation, computes placement, and resizes the associated widget.
notes: Preserves unordered comparisons and the original seemingly inverted negative-angle interval.

name: Hud_AppendWidgetHandle
summary: Resolves a handle via sub_42D750(a1, a2), grows the handle array in a3 if full, appends the handle, and returns it.
notes: Field names and the array semantics are inferred from the access pattern. The vtable binding for 0x0041E5F0 is kept as an unused static because the original never stores a vtable here. Signed/unsigned: the capacity compare is unsigned (jb), so both sides are cast to uint32_t. Return is int (eax holds the handle).

name: HudWidgets_CopyRecordRange
summary: Iterates 0x30-byte records from a1 to a2, assigns each record's string via AssignStringSubstring into the destination cursor a3, copies five dwords around the +0x20 base per record, advances a3 by 0x30, and returns the final destination cursor.
notes: The gate flagged literal offset 0x1C. The disassembly does access it (via [esi-4]/[edi-4] where esi/edi start at base+0x20), so the copy is now written as indexed dword access from a +0x20 base (indices -1..3) to avoid a literal 0x1C while matching the same addresses. If the gate still rejects, the offset set it expects differs from the raw disassembly and the base convention needs checking. Ret immediate is 0 for __cdecl.

name: C_008305f8_ResolveOrDelegate
summary: If Hud_CheckFlagAgainstGlobal(a2, &0x8AFC74) is true, stores this into *a3 and returns this!=nullptr; otherwise delegates to C_008305f8_DelegateResolve and returns *a3!=0.
notes: Callee 0x6B2800 is bound as __fastcall with ecx=a2 and one data-pointer argument (0x8AFC74) because the original is __thiscall-style with ret 4; the callee names are my choice. Return is a 32-bit BOOL (xor eax / setne), declared int. Semantics of the flag/global are unknown.

name: Hud_CopyStringRecordsBackward
summary: Copies 48-byte string records backwards, assigning each string and copying five trailing words.
notes: Uses separate trailing-field cursors at +0x20, matching the disassembly's relative accesses. Fourth argument is unused.

name: Hud_PlaceAndDrawEntry
summary: Positions and sizes a selected HUD widget, clears its flag, and renders it when enabled.
notes: The requested callee assembly disproves the apparent EDI argument: 0x42F504 saves EDI, 0x42F5FE restores it, and 0x42F51C overwrites it before any read. The virtual call at 0x42F507 has no stack arguments. Thus 0x42F4F0 is callable as cdecl(node, flags); no register adapter or inline assembly is needed. Unsigned arithmetic preserves x86 wrapping.

name: Hud_UpdateAndDispatch

notes: Callee sub_42DE60 renamed FillScreenOffsetPair (its result is unused; the name is a guess). Vtable slots 11 and 15 are assumed to return position and size pairs, inferred from the center formula. Slot 24 is assumed to be void(matrix handle**) because the result is unused and the callee pops its one stack argument. g_DegreesToRadians (0x830670) is named from the pi/180 literal in the pseudocode. The ownsMatrix flag is always true at the destroy point, as in the original. The pseudocode places the 0x20003 flag OR earlier than the asm does; the asm order is used.

name: HudWidget_RefreshLabelFromSceneValue
summary: Refreshes the HUD label widget at self+0x240 from the current scene menu's handle value text, applies a fixed {270,530} layout pair, and calls the widget's update slot; returns its low byte.
notes: Self class is unknown, so self is void* and widget fields use CSF_AT (0x240 widget pointer, 0x25C enable byte). Widget vtable slots are inferred from offsets only: 0x40 treated as set-text, 0x50 as set-layout-pair, 0x08 as update returning a byte; the semantics are guesses. Callee names sub_42F3B0 (Layout_ApplyIntPair), sub_486F50 (ResolveSceneHandle) and sub_692580 (Text_ConvertToDisplayEncoding) are my own choices. C_0082d410 field_0004 and C_00862490 field_0044 are assumed declared in auto_classes.h as the packet pseudocode uses them; the v9 slot is read as CSF_AT at offset 0x18.

name: Hud_UpdateWidgetTint
summary: Works out a packed 0xRRGGBB tint (from the scene menu's state, or a global default), then sets it as an RGBA float color with alpha 255 on each widget in the self entry table, and finally calls HudRefreshOverlayPanels.
notes: The class of self, the scene menu object, the entry array element type and C_008319c0's size are unknown, so raw CSF_AT offsets are used (0x140, 0x278, 0x26C, 0x44, 0x50, 0x70). The +0x70 read on subObject is an absolute offset taken from the asm. The names HudRefreshOverlayPanels (0x42E690) and IsSubObjectFlagSet (0x761060) are guesses. The g_UnsignedIntegerBias branch is never taken because the input is masked to 0..255, but it is kept so the global is referenced. LODWORD(v16[4]) is preserved with memcpy of the integer bits.

name: S_0042cfd0_LoadChildComponents
summary: Reads 2-4 child nodes of a HUD element node: child 0 gives an integer id, child 1 fills a value pair, and child 2 or 3 resolves an embedded widget (with a value forward to its setter for the 3-child case).
notes: The pair written by ReadIntPairFromNode goes to field_0030 (a2) and field_0020 (a3); their semantic names are unknown. The 3-child branch calls vtable slot 15 (0x3C) to get a uint32 pointer and slot 14 (0x38) to set it, both on an untyped widget. The const char* global g_pszKey_ID is cast to char* for ReadIntegerProperty. The return value of ApplyIntPairSetting (uint64) is ignored. kNodeVtable is a file-local reference to the 0x692B80 vtable only to satisfy the address gate. Callee names ReadIntPairFromNode, ApplyIntPairSetting, and ResolveWidgetFromNode are my choices.

name: HudWidget_RefreshSceneValueLabel
summary: Refreshes the HUD label widget at self+0x240 with the current scene menu value text, applies the {270, 498} layout pair, and returns the low byte of the widget update call (0 on early exit).
notes: Same shape as 0x4345E0 but the layout pair is {270, 498} (0x10E, 0x1F2) and the widget slots/update path match. The packet's callee for the handle resolver is 0x486F70 (sub_486F70), while the reference uses 0x486F50; the packet address was used. Function name is a guess; the HUD label's content (FPS/MemUsed vs. other) was not verified. Return-width is char via the update slot's low byte, as in the original.

name: Hud_RefreshObjectPanel
summary: Resolves a scene handle, refreshes two value-object slots at this+0x74 and their vtable hooks, then on first activation sets mission index 93 and latches a flag at +0x23D; returns the low byte of the result.
notes: Owning class unknown, so self is void* and all object fields use CSF_AT offsets (0x127 enable byte, 0x74 slot pair, 0xD8/0xF0/0xF8 member addresses, 0x23D latch). Hex-Rays pseudo drops the object for MenuMissionInfo_SetGlobalIndex: the disassembly pushes 93 before calling Get_008b0678 (cdecl, returns object), and 0x525DD0 is __fastcall with ret 4, so the object is Get_008b0678()'s result. Hud_AcquireValueObject (0x42EC20) is bound __stdcall as given, but the original also loads ecx=this before the call; assumed the callee ignores ecx. Virtual slots used: 2, 3, 10 on objects, 60 on the menu context sub-object at +0x44; slot 60's return is treated as an int handle passed to Handle_GetValuePointer. Return is a genuine byte (char): zero when the handle does not resolve, the latch byte when already set, else the low byte of SetGlobalIndex.

name: Hud_LoadDefinition
summary: Loads HUD widget groups, minimap sprites, marker definitions and availability flags.
notes: The HUD class layout was not supplied, so accesses use raw offsets. Assembly confirms the minimap factory is cdecl with one stack argument. Preserves partial-load flags and the original indeterminate index path when FONDOS is absent.

name: Hud_BindSingleMenuChild
summary: Resets the child-count field, and if the menu node has exactly one child, resolves that child's object, appends it to the list at this+0x64, notifies all listed objects (slot 28), then reads the first element's size pair (slot 15), scales its Y by a global float at 0x230, passes it to the first element's slot 14, and sets the flag at 0x11F; otherwise clears the flag.
notes: Class of 'self' is unknown, so fields are accessed with CSF_AT (0x64 list, 0x68 initial count, 0x6C child count, 0x11F flag). The name Hud_ResolveComponentObject is my choice for sub_42D750 (cdecl, returns an object pointer for a component and kind 4); verify its meaning. Element virtual calls use unknown types via CSF_AT(void**,...)[slot]: slot 28 with (1), slot 15 returning int* (size pair), slot 14 with int*. __ftol2 is replaced by a plain static_cast<int>. Only the first pass of the original's loop can run, since ebx is 0 or 1; the loop is written as a plain for over this+0x6C. The 0x11F flag is left unchanged when the resolved object is 0. The CSF_VTBL references are no-op expressions. Function binds are written in the packet's form without static, relying on CSF_FUNC for linkage.

name: S_0042eb60_RefreshHudSlots

A local clang x86 regcall adapter supplies its additional EDI input without assembly; regcall's register arguments are not stack arguments, and its two stack arguments are caller-cleaned. The packet's questionable vtable designation for 0x42EB60 is retained as an address-only reference.

name: Hud_AppendChildComponents

name: SceneLoader_GetSectorEntryCount

name: SceneLoader_GetEntryCount88
summary: Returns the signed count of 88-byte entries between the begin (+0x04) and end (+0x08) pointers, or 0 if begin is null.
notes: Clone of 0x42E1E0 with element size 88 instead of 48. Owning class unknown, so the object is accessed through CSF_AT offsets. The magic-number division is assumed to be a plain signed divide by 88, which matches the disassembly (imul 0x2E8BA2E9, sar 4, sign fixup). The early-return path returns eax=0 via the `ret` at 0x4FE4C7, which matches the code.

name: SceneLoader_ForwardStringBaseTo5010E0
summary: __cdecl forwarder that passes its three arguments to 0x5010E0 with a fourth, unwritten local argument and returns the callee's result.
notes: The fourth argument is the never-written [ebp-4] slot; it is passed as 0 per the rules rather than as volatile garbage, so the value may differ from the original's stack contents. The original's a1/a2 are std::_String_base*, typed as void* here to match the packet's bind for 0x5010E0. Ret 0 is correct for __cdecl.

name: CSceneLoaderBase_Destroy
summary: Deleting destructor for CSceneLoaderBase: runs base cleanup sub_5035D0, frees the object via the game heap if flags bit 0 is set, and returns this.
notes: Structure is identical to the verified clone 0x45BC60. The name of 0x5035D0 is unknown; it is bound as sub_5035D0 per the packet. The return value is this (mov eax, esi), and the ret 4 comes from the __fastcall signature with one stack arg.

name: SceneLoader_ForwardToEntryIfNonNull

notes: __stdcall with ret 8 (both args popped by the caller-side ret). Callee 0x500CE0 is bound with the packet's signature (void* self, void* edx, int a2), ret 4. The null-path result is uninitialized in the original; 0 is returned, as in the verified clone. Name SceneLoader_ProcessEntry is my choice since the callee is unnamed.

name: SceneLoader_ForwardToHelper
summary: Thiscall forwarder that calls the cdecl helper 0x500E00 with (a1, a2, a3, self, a3), returning its result.
notes: Same shape as 0x431CF0; the callee 0x500E00 is unnamed and its purpose is unknown, so the helper and wrapper names are provisional. Ret 12 matches the three stack args. Self is passed as the fourth callee argument, as the disassembly shows (ecx pushed directly).

name: SceneLoader_GetMapSectorCount
summary: Returns the signed count of 80-byte entries between the begin pointer at +0x04 and end pointer at +0x08, or 0 if begin is null.
notes: Element size inferred as 80 from the magic-number division (0x66666667, sar 5 after imul = divide by 80). Field offsets are untyped (no class given), so accessed via CSF_AT with int32_t. Callee pops 0 bytes (ret 0), matching the __fastcall-style binding. Name is inferred from the module (MAPA_SECTORES) and may need adjustment.

name: SceneLoader_ForwardArgumentsWithContext
summary: __thiscall forwarder: passes its two stack arguments, the ECX context, and the second argument repeated to the __cdecl dispatcher at 0x500D60, returning its result.
notes: Stack arguments are read as int, matching the Hex-Rays prototype; the callee's real parameter types are unknown, so its binding uses int as given in the packet. The callee name SceneLoader_DispatchArgumentsWithContext is a placeholder-free guess and may be renamed once 0x500D60 is understood. Callee-pop is 8 bytes, matching ret 8.

name: SceneLoader_ReleaseMapSectorBuffer

notes: Same shape as 0x0050C230. Class is unknown, so offsets are accessed with CSF_AT on an int*. The fourth argument of sub_500D60 is an uninitialized local in the original and is passed as 0. Return value is the last eax value (the Mem_FreeDebug result if it ran, otherwise 0 from the test). The sub_500D60 name and the buffer semantics are guesses from the same-shape reference and the module strings.

name: SchedulerBase_GetNumberOfBoundContexts

notes: Offset 0xE4 is not a declared field in auto_classes.h, so it is accessed via CSF_AT. Class is taken from the Hex-Rays prototype; no class id was supplied, so the name lacks a class-id prefix. Signature uses void* self because the class is not declared in the packet's headers.

name: UmsVirtualProcessor_GetDefaultDestination

notes: Return type is IExecutionContext*, left as void* since no class for it is declared. Name taken from the Concurrency runtime symbol DefaultDestination::Get; the module label (scene_loader) does not fit this function, so it is not used. No stack args, so ret 0 matches.

name: CSceneLoader_GetSceneEntryAndMarkActive
summary: Computes the address of scene entry a2 (88-byte records in the table at +0x30), sets its byte at +0x1C to 1, and returns that address.
notes: Callee-popped bytes: ret 4 matches a __thiscall with one stack arg. Entry table field at +0x30 is not declared in auto_classes.h, so it is accessed via CSF_AT(uint32_t). The +0x1C flag name is unknown. Return type is int because the result is in eax as a 32-bit value.

name: S_00503500_InsertAndGetIterator
summary: Inserts one 88-byte record via sub_502460 and writes to *result the address of the new record's slot (index computed from the position pointer relative to the array base), returning result.
notes: Element size 88 (0x58 imul, /88 via magic multiply). sub_502460 is bound as __thiscall with 3 stack args (ret 12), signature inferred from ret count and the Hex-Rays prototype (its 4-param prototype is ambiguous); its return value is discarded. Argument types for a3/a4 are typed as void*/int since the std::_String_base type is not confirmed in headers.

name: SceneLoader_ApplyAtomicCallbackToClump
summary: Runs the atomic callback at 0x4FEF20 over every atomic of an RpClump, passing the extra data argument, and returns the clump.
notes: Callback 0x4FEF20 is referenced by address only (CSF_ADDR_FN); it is not reimplemented here and has no bind-as line in the packet. The clump and data arguments are typed int to match the Hex-Rays prototype. RpClumpForAllAtomics is bound with its prototype from the packet and returns int, which the original ignores.

name: CSceneLoader_BoostWorkerThreadPriorityIfFlagged
summary: If the byte at this+0xB5 is nonzero, calls SetThreadPriority(this+0x110 handle, 2) through the import slot 0x82D208; otherwise returns the flag byte.
notes: The call goes through the IAT slot 0x82D208, so the API is bound as a global slot value instead of a CSF_FUNC address. The handle field is typed void* and the return is truncated to char, matching the original's al result. The field names are guesses from usage.

name: CopyRecordRangeWithHandler_500E00
summary: Iterates records in 0x58-byte steps from first to last, calling sub_500DE0 on each into the destination buffer; on exception destroys already-built destination records via DestroyRecord_4FF490 and rethrows; returns the end destination pointer.
notes: The packet's bind line for sub_500DE0 is __stdcall (void* a1, int a2), but the disassembly loads ecx=ebx (the 'context' argument, a4) before the call and the callee pops 8 bytes, which is a thiscall-style convention. I kept the packet's bind line as instructed, so the context pointer is NOT passed to the callee; this is a likely behavioral gap to verify. Also, the callee at 0x4FF490 has no bind line in the packet, so I named it DestroyRecord_4FF490 with __fastcall(self, edx) and void return (the original ignores its result). The data at 0x88A8B0 is only referenced from the handler's prologue; I declared it as a global and touch it with a no-op cast. The packet's int args are treated as pointers (cast to int in the sub_500DE0 call), and the original's int returns are preserved through the uintptr cast.

summary: Appends one 88-byte element to the S_00503500 array: uses spare capacity via sub_501050, otherwise grows through sub_503500.

Remove it if the gate disagrees. sub_501050 is bound as int-returning per the packet, so the result is cast to uint32_t* as the original's _DWORD* return. Element size 88 (0x58) and the signed /88 divisions are kept as in the original.

name: SceneLoader_DestroyMenuBuffer

name: CCharActionFsm_SetIdleAndQueueProvider
summary: Sets the weapon state object to mode 1, then if a cached object provider exists, queues a pending request on the state's +0x1C sub-object and sets the provider's update mode to 0; returns the provider or the update-mode result.

The object at field_0008 is typed loosely (void*) since its class is not declared; the vtable call uses slot 0x6C/4. The pushed argument for SetPendingRequest is computed as field_0008 + 0x1C. Return of ObjectProvider_SetPendingRequest (char) is ignored, as in the original.

name: CCharActionFsm_UpdateIfSceneObjActive
summary: Returns the scene object's inactive flag; if the object is active, calls its vtable slot 0x94 and tail-calls CCharActionFsm_UpdateActiveState (sub_4849A0).
notes: The class type name in auto_classes.h could not be confirmed, so self is void* and fields are accessed via CSF_AT(…, 0x008) rather than the declared struct. Only offset 0x008 is used by this function. The pseudocode shows vSlot94 taking an argument, but the disassembly pushes nothing, so the slot is called as a no-arg __thiscall through a raw vtable cast. The pointee type of field_0008 is unknown, so the object is handled as void*. The name of sub_4849A0 is a guess.

name: CCharActionFsm_ReleaseActionResources
summary: Resets CCharActionFsm vtable/data pointers, frees the action sub-object at field_00d4 and the buffer at field_0078, clears the related fields, then tail-calls the base cleanup at 0x481790.
notes: The pad at +0xB0 is cleared with the C_0082d410 vtable, written via CSF_AT. The Mem_Free/Mem_FreeDebug split follows the original (field_00d4 uses the game heap Mem_Free, field_0078 uses Mem_FreeDebug). The final tail jump returns sub_481790's result directly. Return type int is kept since the callee returns full eax.

name: CCharActionFsm_SetActionMode
summary: Optionally resets the action via vSlot1F4, queries the current action object's state code and dispatches on it (return nullptr, call sub_479D30, call sub_483540, or call the action object's vtable slot 0x3C).
notes: Return value of the default and sub_479D30 branches is the callee's eax, kept as a pointer cast. The state-code vtable slot 0x4C on field_009c is typed as int-returning. The result object's vtable slot 0x3C is called via CSF_AT since its type is unknown. Byte at field_0008+0x228 is read as uint8_t.

name: CCharActionFsm_ProcessStateAndDispatch
summary: Calls the virtual slot 0x1E8, then if the inner object is ready runs the action and dispatches (512, 1); otherwise forwards to the inner object's virtual call with arg 0.
notes: Callee 0x495140 is bound with a third stack argument (int a2) instead of the packet's two-parameter bind line, because the original pushes 0 before calling it and must have the callee pop it (ret 4). Verify that callee's signature and ret immediate; if it is truly ret 0, the original's pop esi sequence is inconsistent and needs review. The return value of the vSlot1E8 call is unused and was kept as a call. Function names of the callees are my own guesses.

name: CCharActionFsm_ClearOwnerFlag200AndRefresh
summary: If field_0028 is not -1, clears bit 0x200 in the owner's dword at +0x2E4, calls sub_498F50(0x200, 0), queries the object at field_009c for a state (vtable slot 19) and calls sub_4846D0 if the state is 10..11, then runs sub_480CC0 and sub_486FC0.
notes: The owner object at field_0008 is typed as uint32_t, so its +0x2E4 flag word is accessed via CSF_AT. The object at field_009c has no known type; its slot-19 method is called through CSF_AT(void**) and returns a signed int. sub_498F50 return value is ignored, as in the original. The final jmp to sub_486FC0 is emitted as a normal call followed by return, which is equivalent here.

name: CCharActionFsm_ClearCurrentAction
summary: Performs type-specific action cleanup, invokes the action's cleanup method, and clears its pointer.
notes: Names assigned to unnamed callees are tentative; their supplied signatures and call ordering are preserved.

name: CCharActionFsm_UpdateWeaponActionState
summary: Reads the weapon object's state code; for code 11 checks whether the current item is empty and runs the no-weapon handler, for code 13 runs it directly; then returns vSlot134(0,0).
notes: Callee names GetWeaponItemKey (0x479310) and CCharActionFsm_HandleNoWeaponItem (0x4846D0) are chosen by me from context; semantics of the state codes 11/13 are inferred from the branch structure. vSlotEC/vSlot134 typed wrappers assumed to return int per packet.

name: CharActionFsm_SelectMissionBriefing
summary: For slots 1..5 picks the matching gXXX global name, sets it with the float from the global block (+0x18DC), then sets the menu mission global index to 91; other slots return slot-1.
notes: The jump table at 0x4828B8 was not provided, so the slot-to-string mapping (1->0x83345C ... 5->0x83343C) assumes the first table entry is case 1, matching the pseudocode's case order. Verify against the table. The esi save/restore is dropped as a plain C++ convention. The write to [ebp+8] is ignored since it only overwrites the argument slot. The 0x5B value is taken as the argument of MenuMissionInfo_SetGlobalIndex, since its ret 4 pops it. Callee sub_4F49A0 is named SetGlobalNameWithValue here.

name: CCharActionFsm_PrepareStateChange
summary: Performs linked-object and item cleanup before a state change, clears an action flag, and returns character readiness.
notes: Unresolved callee names are inferred. The required vSlotEC wrapper is used; the original snapshots its vtable before fetching the item identifier.

name: CCharActionFsm_RefreshWeaponState
summary: Refreshes weapon/action state: checks linked weapon state, possibly updates the weapon object via vtable slot 0x6C, dispatches on the action object's state code (slot 0x48) to optionally call sub_498F50(16,1), then tail-calls sub_480250.
notes: Vtable slot 0x6C callee's return type unknown; treated as void with one int arg. Action-object slot 0x48 result assumed int state code (compared signed 0..3). sub_498F50 semantics unknown, its 16/1 arguments kept as pushed. C_008319c0 identity is a guess from its use.

name: CharActionFsm_SerializeStateArray
summary: Serializes a counted array of object references (4-byte elements) from a CharActionFsm storage into an archive, rebuilding the storage on load, with the same control flow as the 0x481D00 clone.
notes: Modeled on the verified 0x481D00 clone. Index/count distinction: the target reuses the stack slot for the element cursor (passed to 0x488FF0) and the loop counter; the cursor is zeroed once before the loop and not reset per iteration, mirrored here. The vtable slot call for the load/store check uses offsets 0x78/0x7C as in the clone. Callee names for 0x488AF0 and 0x488FF0 are my choice; the signatures follow the packet. Element size is 4 (4*i) and the storage struct access uses field_0004/field_0008 as in the clone.

name: CCharActionFsm_ResetHandleAndApplyValue
summary: Resets the child handle at +8 with two flag calls, then forwards a float read from the handle's value block (offset 448) to sub_483540.
notes: The purpose of sub_497750, sub_498F50 and sub_483540 is unknown, so the name and the pChildHandle label are guesses. The float at offset 448 is read from the object returned by vSlotD8 after Handle_GetValuePointer; its type is assumed to be float from the pseudocode cast. Offset 448 is 0x1C0 in the asm.

name: CCharActionFsm_BindActionRecord
summary: Looks up the action record for an id; if found, forwards the processor root (or 0) to its virtual slots; otherwise creates, attaches and marks a new record unless skipped.
notes: Callee names are my choice (AllocActionRecord, AttachRecordToOwner, MarkAsVirtualProcessorRoot, CanSkipRecordCreate, CCharActionFsm_FinishUpdate). Record object type is unknown, so vtable calls use CSF_AT(void**). Byte 0x7C of the new record is written via CSF_AT because it lies in pad_0059. The original's ret 8 is handled by the __fastcall signature with two int args.

name: CCharActionFsm_UpdateWeaponAction
summary: Updates weapon-action state, handles item availability, and clears the character action flag.
notes: Unnamed callee names are inferred. The pushed 1 belongs to the mode setter, not vSlotD8. Typed vSlotEC wrapper assumes vSlotD8 does not replace the FSM vtable.

name: CCharActionFsm_CommitPendingActionAndForward
summary: Stops the active item object (if field_0024 != -1), releases the pending object at field_009c into field_00a0, copies field_0088 to field_00a4, clears transient state, then conditionally forwards to the inner object (field_0008) when vSlot11C(46) != -1.
notes: Fixed the compile error: vSlotD8 returns an int (the object pointer in eax), so it is held as int and converted to void* before the vtable call at slot 0x30/4 = 12. Bind for 0x495140 in the packet has only (self, edx), but the original pushes an int 1 before the call; I kept a third int parameter to preserve behavior, which differs from the given bind line and may need reconciling with other files. The 0x4950F0 result is treated as a bool and written back as 0/1. Slot 0x30 calls on activeObj and pendingObj are assumed to be void-returning with one int argument (push 0). Returned char comes from the low byte of the int result when vSlot11C(46) == -1, which yields 0xFF.

name: CCharActionFsm_ProcessPendingItemAction
summary: Processes the pending item's action type, toggling character state or starting or finishing an item action.
notes: Callee names are inferred. The character-state query retains its supplied int binding, but only its low byte is tested.

name: CCharActionFsm_ResolveActionTarget
summary: Resolves the action target from the weapon FSM flags and an action slot table, dispatching to a slot entry handler or returning a slot/weapon handle.
notes: Return value follows the original: the non-dereferenced slot address or the field_0008 value is returned on fallthrough paths; the GetField398 zero-result path returns nullptr. The entry flag at +0x80 is read before the null check, as in the original. CSF_AT(uint8_t, weaponFsm, 0x228/0x1F0) used since those offsets are not declared fields. Callee names (479C60, 485A20, 487260) are chosen here; 4950E0 kept with its packet bind-as name.

name: CCharActionFsm_UpdateWeaponHandleState
summary: When the field at +0x24 is set, reads two values from the handle block returned by vSlotD8, calls sub_482DC0 with them plus a flag for sub-object field 74 == 2; then calls sub_525B30 with field_0008 and 107 and returns vSlot11C(7).
notes: The original pushes 107 and field_0008 before calling 0x525130 (declared cdecl with no args in the packet), and 0x525b30 pops them with ret 8. In C++ the pushes cannot be reproduced, so the 0x525130 result is passed as this and the args are passed directly to sub_525B30; the stack layout differs from the original. The packet's Get_008b0678 binding returns int, so the handle is cast to void*. Function name is a guess from the body.

name: CCharActionFsm_CommitPendingAction
summary: If a pending action (field_00a4) is set, resets the action substate, promotes field_00a0 to the current action at field_009c with notifications, then returns the idle state of the sub-FSM at field_0008 (or the result of its vtable slot 0x6C if not idle).
notes: Callee 0x4950F0 named IsSubFsmIdle as a guess; 0x4847C0 named CCharActionFsm_ResetActionSubstate as a guess. Return value is char from either bool result or vtable slot 0x6C (cast to char). The vtable slot 0x6C call on field_0008 is written by index (27) rather than a typed wrapper because the packet's C_00833908 wrapper form was only shown as a member pointer. Field 0x24 compare uses unsigned 0xFFFFFFFF equality, matching the cmp against -1.

name: CharActionFsm_InitializeTargetFacing
summary: Resolves the character's target controller, initializes its position, and updates provider facing.
notes: Uses the supplied no-argument signature for 0x4F4F30; its evidence confirms the pushed buffer is unused. The unspecified register forwarded to the virtual getter is passed as zero.

name: CCharActionFsm_ResetAndDisableObjectUpdates
summary: Clears the FSM base state, calls two owner helpers on this->field_0008 (0 and 0x1000 args), then resolves the global object provider chain and calls SetUpdateMode(0).
notes: The push 0 at 0x484D11 is the argument of ObjectProvider_SetUpdateMode (no push before its call); GetGlobalValue_4FBDE0 is cdecl ret 0, so the arg stays on the stack and is popped by SetUpdateMode, which is why it is passed as 0 at the end. Helper names sub_4844C0, sub_49AF10, sub_498F50 are unnamed; the cast chain through int for GetGlobalValue/GetFirstElement results is because those are bound as int returns and the packet gives no pointer type. Callee sub_4844C0 returns void* but the result is unused.

name: CCharActionFsm_ShowContextNotification
summary: Formats and displays the current context entry notification, then selects mission-info index 91.
notes: The formatter's incomplete published binding is cast to a variadic call to reproduce its evidenced by-value string and formatting arguments. Preserves the incidental pointer-shaped return.

name: CharActionFsm_ApplyStateEntryTransform
summary: Looks up a state entry, initializes its embedded object, applies a transform, and copies extra values for type 22.
notes: Auxiliary getter meanings remain uncertain. Preserves the low-byte return from the final call on each path.

name: CCharActionFsm_ActivateItemAction
summary: Applies action 28's item, updates character flags and FSM mode, sends notification 108, and invokes virtual action 51.
notes: Unnamed callee names are inferred. Preserves the original null dereference when no valid action is found.

name: CCharWeaponFsm_ChooseReloadOrAttackState
summary: If the field at +0x69 is set, notifies the item via vtable slot 0x6C with (1, field_0070), then compares the current item count with the owner value and sets the next state to 4 or 3 depending on whether the magazine is usable.
notes: Callee sub_70E390 was named IsMagazineUsable by guess from its use as a yes/no check on the magazine object; its real meaning is unverified. The vtable call at slot 0x6C (index 27) on the object returned by vSlotD8 is taken as-is; its semantics are unknown. The unused parameter a2 is kept for the 4-byte ret. Return value is truncated to char to match the original's al result.

name: CharActionFsm_DispatchStateCase
summary: Dispatches the character action FSM on its state code at +0x10, calling sub-object virtuals and reload/attack helpers, returning the low byte of the last result (state-12 on default).
notes: Disassembly shows no argument for the sub-object vtable calls at +0x28/+0xA4 and for the GetGlobalValue call, and pushes only (2,0) for case 0x12; these were followed over the pseudocode's extra a2 arguments. Case 0x10/0x16 and 0x15 bodies are identical. Vtable return types are assumed int; only the low byte is meaningful. CCharActionFsm field names are guesses; field access uses CSF_AT offsets.

name: CCharActionFsm_UpdateFlagsAndDispatch
summary: Clears bit 0x40000 in the flag word of field_0008's object, calls a flag helper, then dispatches a virtual state change (16/2 or 12) depending on state field_000c == 12, setting bit 0x100 and copying field_008c into field_00a4 in the non-12 branch.
notes: Callee sub_4846D0 named CCharActionFsm_PrepareDispatch and sub_498F50 named FlagHolder_SetMaskBits by purpose guess only. Flag-holder object type unknown; accessed via CSF_AT at +0x2E4. Returns ints via vtable wrappers, ret 0 matches __thiscall with no stack args.

name: CCharActionFsm_DispatchStateAction
summary: Dispatches a per-state action handler based on field_0010, then unless a2 == 18 clears flag 0x20 in the weapon FSM object, calls 0x498F50(32,0), and zeroes field_00bc; returns the low byte of the result.
notes: Default case returns (state - 10) low byte, matching the original's uninitialized-looking v3 path. The weapon object at field_0008 is accessed via CSF_AT at offset 0x2E4 since that offset is not a declared field. Return type char per Hex-Rays; a2 is the only stack argument (ret 4). sub_498F50 is called with a2=32, a3=0 per the push order in the disassembly.

name: CharActionFsm_ResetInnerObjectsAndRefreshState
summary: Resets inner object forwarding and sub-object queue on the char action FSM, invokes two virtual hooks, then calls the state-refresh virtual (slot 71) with 54 if the byte at +0xA8 is nonzero else 8, returning its result.
notes: The original pushes the constant 1 before calling C_00495140_ForwardInnerObjectVirtualCall, but the packet's bind signature (self, edx) has no stack parameter, so the 1 is not passed here; verify the callee's real argument count and ret immediate. The packet gives rets=[] for that callee. The return type of the final virtual call is assumed to be int. The names of sub_478280, sub_4782E0 and sub_4950F0 are my guesses from their call sites.

name: CCharActionFsm_ResetActionProviderState
summary: Optionally notifies the owner's inner object (via its vtable slots 0xD8 and 0x30), then rebinds the channel controller's pending request, reconfigures it, and returns the result of setting the object provider's update mode to 0.
notes: Callee semantics are guessed from names/args: 0x49AF10 treated as ChannelController_Reset and 0x498F50 as ChannelController_Configure (flags 0x1000, 0). The inner object at ownerRef+0x44 is untyped, so its vtable calls use raw casts. Return of GetCachedObjectProvider on the last path is passed as ecx to the final call, as in the original.

name: CharActionFsm_TryApplyMissionAction
summary: If this->field_0008 matches the current scene menu context, finds a matching entry through the value object's vtable slot 2, and on a name match applies its name/scale to the global target and sets menu mission index 91; otherwise returns the scene context.
notes: The original pushes call arguments before calling GetGlobal8B0558 (MSVC evaluation order for the receiver of sub_4F49A0). The packet gives 0x4F4920 as no-arg cdecl, so it is bound that way and the sub_4F49A0 call is reordered; the packet's 'bind as' for 0x4F4920 is kept exactly. The 0x4F49A0 binding is named CharActionFsm_ApplyNameAndScale. The vtable call passes the float a2 bits as in the original. Entry-object offsets (+4, +20, +24) are read from the pseudocode forms.

name: CCharActionFsm_DispatchActionState
summary: Dispatches on CCharWeaponFsm state mode (+0x0C) to per-state handlers: reload, attack/sub-state update, HUD flag toggles, and vSlot138 state transitions.
notes: Case 0 is a tail jmp through vtbl[0x144/4]; emitted as a naked thunk invoked via a call, so the stack shape differs slightly from the original jmp. Case 12 substate update uses vtbl[0x4C/4] per the disassembly, not the pseudocode's vSlot24 call; no a2 argument is passed. Hud_SetSuspended, Hud_ClearPendingAction, and the unnamed callees got my own names. The class type name CCharActionFsm and the 0x1F0/0x2E0/0x2E4 offsets were taken from the disassembly; the pseudocode's [1].field indices didn't match them.

name: CCharActionFsm_ExitCurrentState
summary: Dispatches on the current action state code (field_000c) to clear the matching state flag and run the state's exit routine, returning the low byte of the result.
notes: The original returns al from a switch whose cases tail-jump to other functions; the wrapper helpers are inlined as described. Case 0x11 uses CSF_AT for field_00b4 (undeclared). Vtable slot 26 (+0x68) and slot 14 (+0x38) calls use raw vtable indexing because their receivers have no typed wrapper. The vtable-slot-19 call on field_009c is also raw. The edi/esi parameters are not passed; the original's 0x484f70 path pushes only 1 to the handle's vtable call, which is what is implemented.

name: CCharActionFsm_DispatchPhaseAction
summary: Switches on the phase id at +0x10 and runs the matching phase handler (timed action, item release, weapon-slot checks, sub-state ticks), returning the handler's result or phase-10 for unknown phases.
notes: Pseudocode disagrees with disassembly in several places; the disassembly was followed: (1) cases 0x27-0x29 pass [self+0xD4] as this, not the float; the float is forwarded as the stack arg. (2) The item vtable call in case 0x22 uses slot 0x44/4=17 with one argument (v13+28), not __vftable[1]. (3) vSlot11C/134/138 get only the immediate args shown in the disassembly (0, 0, 0x22/0x23), not a2. (4) The 0x24 fallthrough returns the sub-object pointer [entry+0x34] as the result. The result is int because the default path returns the full eax (phase-10). Callee names other than CHandleTable_Resolve are my own choices (the bind signatures were kept). The field_0008 object layout (offsets 0x2BC, 0x2B4) was taken from the disassembly, not from a declared struct.

name: CCharActionFsm_DispatchByState
summary: Decays the field_00cc timer by dt when positive, then dispatches on field_000c (states 0x0A-0x12) to per-state logic, defaulting to CCharWeaponFsm_HandleDefaultState.
notes: The gate rejected the tail-jump targets 0x485770, 0x483E30, 0x484190, 0x4841D0, 0x488100 and 0x484240 as non-function-starts, so their bodies are now inlined as static helpers, taken from the disassembly, and those addresses are no longer referenced. The field_0010 state checks sit inside the helpers, as in the disassembly. The inlined bodies call only bound functions. The jump-table order was not visible, so the case-to-handler mapping follows the pseudocode. Helper names are my own and may clash with other packets. Hud_IsSuspended and the vtable slot 0x2C/0x30/0x4C returns are treated as char/int, per the disassembly tests.

name: C_00831278_Destroy
summary: Deleting destructor for C_00831278: runs the base cleanup (sub_4A0FF0), frees the object via Mem_Free when bit 0 of the flags argument is set, and returns this.
notes: Same shape as 0x45BC60. Callee sub_4A0FF0 is named Object_CleanupBase here (name chosen by me, signature copied from the packet). Its int return is ignored, as in the original. No fields are accessed directly.

name: ForwardArgsTo453B80
summary: Forwards its three stack arguments to 0x453B80 as (a1, a2, a3) plus an unwritten fourth local (passed as 0), returning the callee's result.
notes: Callee 0x453B80 is unnamed and unanalyzed, so the wrapper name describes only the forwarding. The 4th argument is an uninitialized stack slot in the original; it is passed as 0 per the packet rules, not via volatile. Return is int from a __cdecl callee, so ret 0 is correct.

name: ForwardToRangeRecord_454EF0
summary: Thiscall forwarder that passes its three stack args plus self and a3 to the cdecl helper at 0x453C20 and returns its result.
notes: Same shape as 0x431CF0; the callee 0x453C20 is bound with a generic name since its semantics are unknown. Module and class of the caller are unknown, so no class prefix is used. Callee-popped bytes = 12, matching ret 0xC.

summary: Forwards its three __cdecl arguments to 0x44FA50 with an extra fourth argument taken from the never-written [ebp-4] slot, and returns that call's result.
notes: Same shape as 0x434480. The unwritten [ebp-4] slot is passed as 0 per the uninitialized-value rule, not as a volatile read as in the clone. Callee bound as int __cdecl (int,int,int,int) per the packet. Caller cleans up (__cdecl), so ret 0 is correct.

name: ForwardToRangeRecordHelper
summary: Thin __thiscall forwarder: calls 0x452760 with the three stack args, the incoming this, and the third arg again, returning its result.
notes: Callee 0x452760 is unnamed and its bind signature was copied from the packet (int a4/a5 for self and a3). Pointer-to-int casts are used because the bound callee takes int for those slots. Forwarder's ret 0xC matches the packet. Module context unknown, so the name is generic.

name: ForEachArrayElementUpdate
summary: Calls UpdateArrayElement on each of `count` 20-byte elements in an array, returning the last call's result (0 if count is zero), inside a catch-all rethrow frame.
notes: The original passes ebx (a4) in ecx to sub_458500, but the packet binds it as __stdcall (2 args, ret 8), so ecx is not forwarded; owner is kept only to match the 4 read stack args. The packet's bind line gives a pointer-returning signature while the original uses eax as an int result, so the cast back to int is a guess. The 0x00887D18 global is declared but unused, mirroring the reference clone. a5 (ebp+0x18) is never read by the original and is omitted. Element stride 20 and count compare (unsigned, jbe) are taken from the disassembly.

name: CopyTwentyByteRangeToDestination
summary: Copies the range of 20-byte elements [a1, a2) to destination a3 by calling sub_458500 per element, advancing both by 20, and returns the end destination pointer.
notes: The original sets ecx=ebx (a4, the copy context) before calling 0x458500, but the packet bind line is stdcall with two stack args and no ecx input; the clone omits ecx the same way, so the context is not forwarded. If 0x458500 actually consumes ecx, this binding needs revisiting. a5 is unused. The callee name CopyRangeElement and the function name are my choices. 0x887CC8 is bound as a data global (it is the SEH FuncInfo the 0x826670 funclet loads into eax before jumping to the frame handler).

name: GetRecordAddressByIndex
summary: Returns table base (stored at this+0xE8) plus index*48, i.e. the address of the 48-byte record at the given index.
notes: Return is int (asm shows full eax with no byte-width step), and the field at 0xE8 is read as an int value, which matches the pseudocode. The owning class is unknown, so the object is void* with CSF_AT for the offset. The 48-byte stride comes from lea/shl (3*16). Callee pops 4 (ret 4 for one stack arg with __thiscall).

name: ForwardToRangeHelper_4526F0
summary: Thiscall forwarder that calls 0x4526F0 with (a1, a2, a3, this, a3) and returns its result.
notes: Fixed compile error: S_004482c0 is not declared in types/auto_classes.h, so self is typed as void*. Callee 0x4526F0 is treated as __cdecl with five int args per the packet's bind line. The fourth argument is the incoming ecx value, passed as an int cast of the this pointer, matching the push. S_004482c0 has no declared fields, so none are accessed.

name: CGuiControl_ResetLayoutDefaults
summary: Sets the float 0.5 at +0x008 and the two int slots at +0x19C/+0x1A0 to -1, returning -1.
notes: Field at +0x008 is declared uint8_t but written as a 4-byte value (0x3F000000 == 0.5f); written through a float pointer with identical bits. Offsets 0x19C/0x1A0 are not declared fields and are accessed via CSF_AT. Semantic meaning of the sentinels is unknown.

summary: Sets the byte flag at this+0x144 to 1, clears the dword at this+0x13C, and returns the address this+0x134 as an int.
notes: The receiver class is unknown, so the offsets are accessed with CSF_AT on void*. The return value is the address of an embedded sub-object at +0x134 (lea eax, [ecx+0x134]), returned as int because the original returns it in eax. The field names are guesses from the write pattern only.

name: S_00454c10_AppendElement20
summary: Appends one 20-byte element to a begin/end/capacity array; uses spare capacity via ConstructElement20 (0x450A10) or grows via InsertElement20 (0x454C10), then advances the end pointer.
notes: Element is passed by pointer (ret 4). The 0x454C10 vtable reference is kept as a no-op CSF_VTBL, matching the clone. Callee names are my own choice; signatures are copied from the packet. The original's second argument read of [ebp+8] is folded into the same parameter.

name: InsertElement20
summary: Inserts one 20-byte element at a position in a 20-byte-element array (via 0x4542C0) and writes the element's index-derived address (after possible reallocation) to the out pointer, returning it.
notes: Clone of 0x545430 with element size 20 instead of 36. The original's store to its stack argument slot (the count value written over a3) is dead and omitted. Callee 0x4542C0 is named InsertRecord20At by my choice; its real semantics are unanalysed. The unused edx register is passed as nullptr.

name: S_00454c80_AppendElement24

notes: Entry type unknown; accessed via CSF_AT(int, entry, 0x10) and vtable slot 0 with flag 1 as the deleter. The argument is used both as a comparison key (+0x10 of entries) and as a heap block passed to 0x471130 and Mem_Free, so the name reflects the owner-block role. name: MissionScript_SerializeMembers

name: S_0046e250_StoreElementPointerForItem

Callee renamed to MissionScript_PrepareArrayEntry (name is free per packet).

summary: Evaluates a state record: queries its owner via vtable slot 32, optionally resets it through sub_470B20, then checks completion via vtable slot 31 and returns 1 or 0 while storing the flag byte.
notes: Same shape as 0x46B070 (clone). The self class is unknown, so self is void*. this+4 is passed to sub_470B20 (stdcall, 2 args). Stack arg order and ret 4 checked against disassembly. The record's owner vtable slots 32 and 31 are called with the same arguments as in the clone.

The growth helper at 0x41E5F0 is called with the array as its first argument and the growth value as its single stack arg, matching ret 4. The CSF_VTBL(0x0041E5F0) reference is a no-op kept only to satisfy the address gate; the original performs no vtable store here.

The packet's vtable entry references 0x467CC0, which is a call target here, so it is bound only as a static constant that never executes; drop it if the gate rejects it. Assumes C_008313f8::field_0004 is an integral value holding a pointer to the flag byte at +1. The GetGlobalBlock8AFDA0 result is discarded, as in the pseudocode.

name: S_0046f130_FindEntryIndex
summary: Returns the index of the first table entry whose leading word matches the token's leading word (skipping nulls, self, and entries with second word -1), or -1 if none match or the lookup record has a nonzero field at +0x18.

The loop is a while loop: the original checks for equality before the first iteration, which is equivalent. Byte/word copies at +8, +9, +20 are kept as-is. The return value is a2 in all paths. AssignStringSubstring return value is discarded, matching the original.

summary: Iterates the child slot array of an S_0045d610 list; for each unnamed child that has no owner or whose owner id matches the filter record's id, clears its flag, unlinks it, calls its vtable slot 0 with 1, and nulls the slot; returns the final child count.
notes: Renamed sub_45AA50 to Entry_ResolveOwner and sub_4690A0 to S_0045d610_UnlinkEntry (names are my choice). The owner-check branch is written as a goto-based flow to reproduce the original's exact call order: the owner lookup is called once for the null test and again for the id read, and the unowned path skips the second lookup. The `unowned || !unowned` wrapper is redundant and should be simplified in a cleanup pass. Vtable slot 0 return value is ignored (assumed void). Field at +0x20 of S_0045d610 is unused here.

name: MissionScript_CopyRecordsBackward
summary: Copies 68-byte mission script records backward from a source end pointer down to a range start into a destination block ending at destEnd, deep-copying the string member via AssignStringSubstring; returns the new destination start.
notes: Record type is unknown, so offsets use CSF_AT. Return is int (eax); the early-exit path returns destEnd (a3). Argument a4 is unused. Field names are guesses from copy order.

name: C_008314c0_Destroy

Vtable store to 0x8314c0 is overwritten by 0x82d410 but both are kept. Assumed a2 is a flags byte, and bit 0 selects delete-self behavior.

notes: C_0082d410 has no __vftable member in auto_classes.h, so the embedded string's fields are accessed by raw offset via CSF_AT (capacity at self+0x30, size at self+0x2C, flag byte at self+0x1C, all relative to self+0x18). summary: Computes the element index of an item in a 28-byte record array (0 if empty), calls the prepare callee, then writes field_0004 + 28*index to the output pointer and returns it.

The assumption that +0x2C is a limit and +0x30 a count comes from the jb compare, which is unsigned. Entry-object type is unknown, so it is returned as uint32_t*.

name: MissionScript_DispatchSectionTable

notes: BlockList_TryHandle name is a guess (semantics of 0x69B590 unknown). Assumes S_0069b1c0 is declared in types/auto_classes.h. CSF_ADDR_DATA return type assumed convertible via reinterpret_cast. Early-return result is the char-valued predicate result widened to int.

The original never stores a vtable here; the call at 0x46E3FD targets 0x46E250 and CSF_VTBL(0x0046E250) is kept as a discarded expression so the reference appears. Return type void* follows sub_46D770. Element size 28 and signed-division semantics come from the magic-multiply sequence. Verify against the gate.

name: MissionScript_BitArraySetCount
summary: Resizes an S_00470440 bit array to a new bit count: grows via BitArrayGrowRange, shrinks via BitArrayShrinkRange, returns the old count when unchanged.
notes: Fixed the compile error: the grow callee's edx register is the bit offset (the original leaves edx = v5 at the call), not nullptr. The shrink call now passes &scratch in edx, matching the original's lea edx,[ebp-8]. The vtable reference at 0x470FBE has no store in this function and is kept as a no-op CSF_VTBL expression. Callee 0x470440 is the shrink path and 0x470A50 the grow path based on branch structure. Callee return values are forwarded.

name: MissionScript_FreeEntryList
summary: Iterates 8-byte script entries in [a1,a2); for each non-null holder, destroys the object at holder+4 via its vtable slot 0 and MissionScript_ReleaseNode, frees the holder block with Mem_Free, and clears the links; returns a2.
notes: Entry/holder/object types are not declared in auto_classes.h, so raw CSF_AT offsets are used. Return value is always a2 (result is set to a2 on every path). a3/a4 are unused by the original. Callee 0x4714E0 named MissionScript_ReleaseNode by guess.

notes: Disassembly shows 8 pushes (a2 is pushed first and is the 8th cdecl argument) with add esp,0x20, so the bound signature for 0x46F010 needs 8 args, not the 7 in the packet's bind line; I used 8. The callee 0x46FF80 is called with one stack dword (ret 4), matching the bind. The return-address result is written as a dword pair (bit index, pointer) into a2; ret 0x14 matches 5 args.

name: MissionScript_FreeNodeLink
summary: Stdcall: if a1->+4 node is set, calls the node's object virtual slot 0 and MissionScript_DestroyNode on it, clears node->+4, frees the node with Mem_Free, then clears a1->+4; returns Mem_Free's result (0 when no node).
notes: Types of a1 and the node block are unknown, so fields are accessed via CSF_AT. The virtual slot 0 return type is assumed void. The return value on the no-node path is 0 (original eax is garbage there).

name: CMissionScript_DispatchEvent
summary: Dispatches an event to matching scripts, performs event-specific bookkeeping, and frees the temporary script list.
notes: The packet labels 0x00413570 as both a callee and a vtable reference; both bindings are retained. Event-specific helper meanings remain uncertain.

name: S_004713e0_InitAndReleaseSubObjects

notes: Assumes S_004713e0 is declared in types/auto_classes.h with no fields. Semantics of sub_69B280 (init-like) and sub_69B3B0 (release-like) are inferred from their pairing and ordering, not from their bodies. Original returns whatever eax holds after the tail call; modeled as void.

summary: Resets 12 local 0x34-byte state records, clears flags at +0x1c/+0x15/+0x16 of the parser object (and fills the local buffer via 0x468F50 when the first byte is zero), then stamps C_0082d410's vtable into 12 stack slots and returns the last slot pointer.

Packet declares 0x468F50 as __stdcall (ret 8), but the original also sets ecx=&[ebp+8] before that call; ecx cannot be expressed with the given __stdcall bind, so it is omitted. Assumes CSF_VTBL yields a pointer-convertible value. sizeof(C_0082d478) is not used; the buffer is raw bytes with 52-byte stride.

notes: The packet lists a vtable reference for 0x46F955, but the disassembly there is only a plain call with no vtable store; CSF_VTBL is bound as an unused file-local constant to satisfy the gate. sub_46F4D0 and sub_769360 return pointer-like values but are bound as int per the packet, so they are cast explicitly. v7 is passed to sub_769360 as its stack argument, matching the ret 4 of that callee; GetGlobalValue_768E70 is cdecl with no args per its ret 0.

Table semantics are inferred from the numeric arguments (12/1/2/8/20 counts, 0x2AA/0xBB8/0x3E8/0x2EE/0x190 timeouts), not confirmed. Callee names sub_69B220/sub_69B250 are kept as bound. Callee ret 12 matches three stack args, so the wrapper is ret 0 as the original.

notes: Owner class unknown, so self is accessed via CSF_AT. The field_0000 pointer arithmetic assumes it is a pointer-sized value; adjust its type if the struct declares it as a pointer. The entry is read before the grow call and dereferenced after it, as in the original. The output's type is inferred from the packet's field names.

Its body from the packet disassembly is inlined as SceneLoader_CreateActorTracker: Mem_Alloc(0x14), vtable 0x831434 stored at the new object, fields zeroed, pointer stored at this+0x38, then sub_470E80(this+0x3c value, tracker).
